The options imply an event move of 10.1% (11.26% straddle on the Nov-20 expiry, ATM IV 157%), though the ATM spread is 57% of mid, so treat that as indicative. Skew is +24 vol points toward puts while put/call open interest is 0.25. The last seven reactions have a median absolute move of 4.66% and went up 4 of 7 times (+19.3% Feb-26, +4.7% May-26, -3.4% Aug-26). Run-in: -9.6% over 5 days, -18.8% over 20 days, -50.6% from the $133.81 high on 2026-07-01. That move is the sector's. Over the same windows SOXX did -9.6% and -17.4%, AMKR -8.9% and -20.6%, and SOXX is -36% from its June peak. KLIC has had no adverse company news: the only filings since the call are an Oct-14 8-K changing incentive-plan metrics and Form 4 tax withholdings on RSU vests. The bar for the September quarter is consensus non-GAAP EPS of about $1.41-1.46 on revenue of $375-384M (Earnings Whispers, Benzinga and FXEmpire, around Nov 11). That sits at the midpoint of the August guide ($375M +/- $20M, non-GAAP EPS $1.42, GM about 48%). The whisper is $1.61. No numeric December-quarter consensus was found. In August management said above-average demand would last through at least H1 FY27, POs run into FQ2 FY27, TCB revenue would exceed $100M in FY26 and reach $150-200M in FY27, and H2 FY27 detail would come in November. Short interest is about 2.2M shares (about 4%, 3.7 days to cover, equibles, Nov 13), so it is not crowded.
view: This is a cyclical upswing name that the semis bear market has cut in half without any company-specific news. What KLIC can be checked against since it last spoke is mostly firm. ASE's ATM revenue for October was +7.9% month on month and +57.7% year on year (company release, Nov 10). JCET's Q3 revenue was +10% quarter on quarter. ASMPT posted record Q3 bookings of US$1.13B with record TCB orders and guided Q4 above consensus. That makes a September-quarter beat at or above the midpoint likely, and a December-quarter guide that is flat to up plausible. Three things cut against it. ASMPT guided its SEMI revenue (wire bonders plus TCB) flat for Q4 because advanced-packaging lead times are longer. A new CEO (Raj Talluri, in the job since Sep 1) is holding his first call and has a reason to reset expectations, and FY27 H2 commentary is due on that call. And in this tape back-end peers have not been rewarded for good prints: ASMPT fell 4.3% the day after its record-bookings release and BESI fell after its Q3. At about 11x an annualized $1.4-1.5 quarterly EPS run-rate, the price already discounts a cycle peak. A guide that grows sequentially could produce a relief move, and a flat guide plus a cautious H2 could take the stock down another leg with the sector. The scoring window ends at tomorrow's open, which follows the 08:00 ET call, so both the guide and the call fall inside it. So does overnight sector noise, which for an 80%-vol name is several percent on its own. My lean is slightly to the upside, and not enough to act on.

recommendation.reason: The decline is tied to the sector derating (SOXX -36% from peak, KLIC tracking it 1:1 over 5 and 20 days), not to anything at KLIC. Counterparty data since August (ASE October ATM sales, JCET Q3, ASMPT record bookings) supports a beat and a firm December guide. But ASMPT's flat SEMI guide and the new CEO's first call make the deciding line, the December guide plus FY27 H2 tone, close to a coin flip against a whisper already above the guide range. I cannot show a mispricing beyond a mild upside lean, so there is no recommendation.
recommendation.what_would_flip_it: A December-quarter revenue guide clearly above the September quarter (around $400M or more), with the new CEO confirming FY27 H2 growth and the TCB pipeline, would make me a buyer. A flat-to-down guide or a soft H2 would make the downside likely.

self_critique: The strongest case for going long is that this is a high-beta cyclical at about 11x run-rate EPS. Its own evidence (POs into FQ2 FY27, record TCB bookings industry-wide, OSAT revenue still climbing in October) supports a December guide above the September quarter. And KLIC's history in the upcycle is mostly positive reactions (+10.6%, +19.3%, +4.7%), so 55 may be too timid. The strongest case for going short is that a new CEO has every reason to guide conservatively and talk down H2 FY27. ASMPT's flat SEMI guide hints at a plateau. The whisper ($1.61) is above the top of the guide range, so even a beat can disappoint. And a tape that sold ASMPT on record bookings may sell this too. These offset each other, and neither changes the conclusion that there is no showable mispricing.
approach_notes: P6's instruction to take the run-in apart against peers was the most useful step: it showed the drawdown was the sector's and stopped me from treating it as either a cushion or a warning. P7's advice to estimate the deciding line from counterparties helped, but the counterparties here were split (ASE up, ASMPT SEMI flat), so it ended near 50 honestly.
